title: The enriched DEFAULTS deliberately mark array boundaries with a doubled separator where GAvroSchemaFlattener uses a single one; gAvroParity() matches GAvro
rationale: The second, independent half of the withdrawn parity claim, isolated on an underscore-free schema so the boundary marker is the only variable. GAvroSchemaFlattener has no array-boundary marker at all: its useArrayBoundarySeparator flag globally renames the one separator, so its default joins array element fields with a single _. FlattenOptions defaults to a doubled marker because a visible array boundary is a useful convention and FlattenedField.arrayBoundaries() exists alongside it. The defaults are therefore deliberately not GAvro's, and FlattenOptions.gAvroParity() is the migration path - measured by the twin row enriched-gavro-parity-factory-matches-gavro-across-an-array-boundary on this exact schema and datum.
catchesBugClass: Divergent boundary-marker conventions between two flatteners, and a change to either default. Paired with its twin it also catches the repair being undone: if gAvroParity() were 'simplified' back into the defaults, the twin would go red while this row stayed green, which is exactly the asymmetry that makes the pair readable.
cannotCatch: It cannot show the downstream consequence, that a Spark job migrating flatteners silently produces an all-null column under the new name. It says nothing about which convention consumers actually depend on, which is the question the parity factory exists to let each caller answer for themselves.

predicted.detail: The enriched arm emits items__sku; the GAvro arm emits items_sku. PREDICTION LEFT AS DEFECT ON PURPOSE: the measurement has not moved a byte, only the judgement of it has, so this is a deliberate reclassification recorded as a classificationOverride.

configDescription: assert ENRICHED_KEYSET vs GAVRO_SCHEMA_FLATTENER, default FlattenOptions
